nodes.name: YCloud Webhook
nodes.notes: rawBody ON: the raw body lands in binary.data. $json.body comes REPACKAGED (1.10 -> 1.1) and is NOT usable for signing. See design W-E.

nodes.name: Body To Text
nodes.notes: Turns binary.data into text without parsing it. The native node is used instead of Buffer in a Code node so as not to depend on how n8n stores binaries.

nodes.name: Secret
nodes.notes: W-D: the secret lives in bot.config, not in the workflow JSON. NO alwaysOutputData on purpose (W-I): if the database fails or the row is missing, this has to blow up so n8n answers 500 and fires the Error Manager.

parameters.query: select value from bot.config where name = 'ycloud_webhook_secret';

nodes.name: Prepare Signature
nodes.notes: Does not compute the HMAC: that is the native Crypto node (W-B). Here the header is only parsed and the text to sign is built.

nodes.name: Compute HMAC
nodes.notes: W-B: native node, not crypto.createHmac in a Code node (require depends on the instance allow-list). If the signature does not match, W-E gives the order to rule out causes: first the encoding (hex vs base64), then the secret, and only at the end the body.

nodes.name: Valid Signature?
nodes.notes: The three conditions in AND. The 300 s tolerance (W-C) rejects an old replay even if its signature is authentic.

nodes.name: Reject
nodes.notes: EXPLICIT 401 and a sanitized body: it does not say which of the two conditions failed, which would only save work for whoever is probing. The detail goes to the alert.

nodes.name: Rejection Alert
nodes.notes: INV-15 by another route: see the note on 'Anomaly Alert'. Goes AFTER the Respond node so it does not delay the HTTP response.

nodes.name: Map Status
nodes.notes: W-F. A message WITHOUT externalId is not from the bot (someone sent it from the YCloud inbox): it is ignored silently. The unknown-key alert is kept only for an externalId that is present but not in bot.sends, which is the serious case.

nodes.name: Update Record
nodes.notes: W-H: monotonicity lives in the WHERE, not in an IF - an IF can be disconnected without anything failing. The three statuses that can advance are explicit: delivered and failed are terminal (the first verdict wins) and reviewed belongs to the operator, it is never overwritten. queryReplacement goes as an ARRAY. NO alwaysOutputData (W-I).

parameters.query:
with previous as (
  select status from bot.sends where unique_key = $1
), changed as (
  update bot.sends
     set status        = $2,
         ycloud_id     = coalesce(nullif($3, ''), ycloud_id),
         wamid         = coalesce(nullif($4, ''), wamid),
         error_code    = case when $2 = 'failed' then nullif($5, '') else error_code end,
         error_message = case when $2 = 'failed' then nullif($6, '') else error_message end,
         closed_at     = now()
   where unique_key = $1
     and status in ('pending', 'sent', 'ambiguous')
  returning status
)
select (select status from previous) as previous_status,
       (select status from changed) as new_status;

nodes.name: Accept
nodes.notes: EXPLICIT 200. Also for what was ignored and for what did not advance: if the message arrived and we understood it, the answer is 200 even if nothing was written. The 500 is never fabricated, it is left to fail on its own (W-I).

nodes.name: Anomaly Alert
nodes.notes: INV-15 by another route: parse_mode has NO None option, and omitting it does NOT disable parsing - n8n sends Markdown anyway and a key with an odd number of underscores kills the alert with a 400 (confirmed on 2026-09-08). HTML is set and & < > are escaped: that way the underscore is an ordinary character and no key can kill the alert.
